messages.author: 31dc03607958a62a
messages.subject: Constraints in Parameters lognormal
parts:
Hi Users,

I do model lognormal for response time for to strategies :

First strategy :

Responses times are defined with 2 parameters, beta and tau, with beta-tau > 0.

I want to define mu = beta - tau with constraint mu > 0. But I don't how to define it. When I do le following, the model doesn't run.

data {
  int P;
  int Q;
  real<lower=0> T[P,Q];
  real mulogT;
  real<lower=0> sigmalogT;
}

parameters {
  real tau[P];
  real betaT[Q]; 
  real<lower=0> sigmaT[Q];
}

transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu[P,Q]; But the model doesn't run when I compel mu.
   for(q in 1:Q){
    for(p in 1:P){
     mu[p,q] <- betaT[q] - tau[p];
    }
  }
}

model {
  tau ~ normal(0,1);
  betaT ~ normal(mulogT,sigmalogT);
  sigmaT ~ gamma(.5,.5);
  for(p in 1:P){
    for(q in 1:Q){
      T[p,q] ~ lognormal(mu[p,q],sigmaT[q]);
    }
  }
}

Second Strategy :

I don't compel mu, better, without mu and I transform response time with lognormal

and the 2nd model is below. The problem with this model is that the n_eff of betaT are very small form 5000 iterations although Rhat is closed to 1.
The graphical is joined.


data {
  int P;
  int Q;
  real<lower=0> logT[P,Q];
  real mulogT;
  real<lower=0> sigmalogT;
}

parameters {
  real tau[P];
  real betaT[Q]; 
  real<lower=0> sigmaT[Q];
}

model {
  tau ~ normal(0,1);
  betaT ~ normal(mulogT,sigmalogT);
  sigmaT ~ gamma(.5,.5);
  for(p in 1:P){
    for(q in 1:Q){
      logT[p,q] ~ normal(beta[q]-tau[p],sigmaT[q]);
    }
  }
}

Bests Eric.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constraints in Parameters lognormal
parts:
The lognormal mean/location (mu) isn't constrained to be positive,
only the outcome (T) is.

- Bob
